newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HOECHST SELLS CHEMICAL UNITS TO CLARIANT.
newsitem.headline: HOECHST SELLS CHEMICAL UNITS TO CLARIANT.

text.p: Hoechst South Africa Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to sell part of its Speciality Chemicals Division and its 50 percent stake in Polyrem Ltd to Clariant Southern Africa Ltd, a unit of Switzerland-based Clariant AG for 78 million rand.
The announcement follows Hoechst AG and Clariant AG's decision to combine their speciality chemical interests.

Hoechst SA managing director Steffen Beuthner said that, the company believed the short- and long-term benefits of selling the business outweighed the alternatives of either maintaining the status quo or entering into a similar merged entity.

"...These businesses are core to Clariant and they will derive the critical mass which we lack. There is also the beneficial effect on our gearing as a result of this transaction which reduces from 44 percent to 24 percent," Beuthner said.
The company said that assuming the sale had been effective throughout the year to December 31 1996, Hoechst SA's headline earnings per share would have risen by 11.8 percent to 26.2 cents a share.
Net asset value would have risen 3.7 percent to 253 cents each, it said.
Hoechst SA earlier reported headline earnings of 16 cents a share for the half year to June 30, up from 11.5 cents previously.
